name: 67 (6 7, six seven)
blurb: A shouted "six seven" meme from a 2025 rap song; it has no fixed meaning
title: 67 Meaning: What Does "6 7" (Six Seven) Mean in Slang?
description: "6 7" (six seven) is a 2025 meme from Skrilla's song "Doot Doot (6 7)". It has no fixed meaning: kids shout it with a palms-up gesture as a joke.
answer: "67", said "six seven", does not have a fixed meaning. It is a catchphrase that people, mostly kids and teens, shout or type as an inside joke, often with both palms up moving up and down. It comes from the rapper Skrilla's drill song "Doot Doot (6 7)", which spread through basketball video edits in 2025, and Dictionary.com named it its 2025 Word of the Year.

body: The line comes from "Doot Doot (6 7)" by the American rapper Skrilla, first put out in December 2024 and officially released in February 2025. The song became the soundtrack for short-video edits of basketball players, especially LaMelo Ball, who is listed at 6 feet 7 inches, so the number fit the clips.

From there it jumped to viral clips of young people yelling "six seven", including a boy who became known as the "67 Kid" in spring 2025. By autumn it was being shouted in classrooms and at games, and Dictionary.com picked "67" as its 2025 Word of the Year in October 2025.

body.note: Skrilla himself has said he never put a meaning on it and would not want to. Theories about the number (a street, a police code) are guesses.

body: Most of the time it is a reflex: someone says the number 6 or 7, or anything close to it, and others answer "six seven!" with the hand gesture. Some people also use it like "so-so" or "maybe this, maybe that".

ul: "What page are we on?" "Sixty-seven." "SIX SEVEN!" (the joke is just that the number came up)
"How was the test?" "Honestly? 6 7." (meaning: so-so, could go either way)
"The score's 67 to 60" ... and the whole bench starts doing the hands.
"My little brother says 6 7 to literally everything and I don't know why."

sections.h: Is it a trend or brainrot?
body: Dictionary.com described it as almost impossible to define and grouped it with "brainrot", online humour that is funny because it is meaningless. That is the honest answer: the meaning is the shared joke, not a hidden code. If you are confused, so is everyone over about 15.

sections.h: Tone and when not to use it
body: It is harmless and playful, but it can be annoying, and some teachers have asked students to stop shouting it in class. Adults saying it usually come across as joking about kids' slang. It is not used in writing beyond chats and comments.

faq.a: No. It is not code for anything rude or secret. It is a nonsense catchphrase from a rap song, used as a joke.
Both hands held out palms up and moved up and down in turn, like weighing two things. It often goes with saying "six seven".
The phrase comes from Skrilla's song "Doot Doot (6 7)". Basketball edits of LaMelo Ball, who is 6 ft 7 in, and viral clips of kids shouting it made it a meme in 2025.
